# Use vesting-schedule

<!-- Generated by build_pack_guides.py from pack.json and the skills' own files. Edit those, not this. -->

Work out vesting for founder stock, restricted stock, options and RSUs — each grant's cliff date and amount, every vesting date in whole shares, what is vested on any date, what happens when someone leaves (vested, forfeited or repurchasable, and the last day to exercise), single- and double-trigger acceleration on a sale, and the US 83(b) election deadline moved past weekends and holidays — computed by a script that keeps the totals exact.

**Reach for it when** a founder asks "how much has my co-founder vested", "what happens to her shares if she leaves", "when does the cliff hit", "build our vesting schedule", "when is the 83(b) deadline", or "what does double-trigger acceleration give us in a sale".

## Install it

```bash
npx skilldrop-cli install vesting-schedule                 # Claude Code, your user folder
npx skilldrop-cli install vesting-schedule --project       # Claude Code, this repo
npx skilldrop-cli install vesting-schedule --ide cursor    # or kiro, codex, antigravity, copilot
```

It is part of the Startup legal pack: [`--pack startup-legal`](../packs/use-the-startup-legal-pack.md) installs it with its neighbours.

It ships scripts, so it needs Python 3 (standard library only, nothing to install). What they may touch is declared in [its manifest](../../../packs/startup-legal/skills/vesting-schedule/manifest.json).

## Ask for it

Say it the way you would to a colleague. Requests like these route to it:

- "How much has my co-founder vested if she leaves next month?"
- "When is the 83(b) deadline for the stock we signed last week?"
- "Build the vesting schedule for our first three hires' options"
- "What does double-trigger acceleration give our team if we're acquired?"

Requests like these belong to a different skill, so it shouldn't answer them:

- "How much of the company will I own after the Series A?"
- "Review this employment contract before I send it"
- "What strike price should our options have?"

If another skill answers instead, ask for this one by name: "use vesting-schedule".

## Check what you get

A good result:

- **Every share count and date comes from the computed schedule,** and each grant's dates sum to its shares.
- **A start on the 29th–31st vests on the last day of shorter months,** and leap years count.
- **The 83(b) deadline is an exact date,** moved past weekends and federal holidays, and a passed one is said plainly.
- **Leaving gives vested, unvested and the exercise deadline,** each from the leaving date, not today.
- **Every assumed term is stated,** with the other reading's figure when it changes the answer.
- **The reply answers the question first,** with no mention of scripts or files.

## Use something else when

- Tax: what an 83(b) or an exercise costs, ISOs against NSOs, EMI or ESOP rules
- Ownership after a funding round: that's a cap table
- Drafting the stock purchase or option agreement
- Valuing the shares or setting a strike price
